content.text: The evidence clearly points to pricing.io-internal.svc, an internal dependency owned by checkout-platform, becoming slow (1500ms calls) starting exactly at the onset. No deploys occurred on io-shop itself in this window.

hypotheses.subject: io-pricing
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's latency and error spike began when calls to its internal pricing dependency (pricing.io-internal.svc) started taking 1500ms consistently, saturating request latency (p50/p95/p99 jumped from ~45/220/380ms to ~1545/1715/1890ms) and causing client disconnects on the account page. No deployment or config change was recorded for io-shop in this window, and the register shows io-pricing is internally owned (checkout-platform), so the fault lies in that dependency rather than in io-shop's own code.

supporting_evidence.claim: 2026-09-26T18:17:00Z WARN io-shop: slow upstream call - pricing.io-internal.svc took 1500ms for /v1/shoppers/shopper-20294-4-0/basket-total (25 of 200 requests)
2026-09-26T18:18:00Z WARN io-shop: slow upstream call - pricing.io-internal.svc took 1500ms for /v1/shoppers/shopper-43652-9-0/basket-total (200 of 200 requests)
p50_ms jumped from 44 to 1544-1546 and p95_ms from ~215 to ~1710-1723 starting at 2026-09-26T18:18:00Z
io-pricing: internal, owned by checkout-platform, at pricing.io-internal.svc - What a shopper's basket comes to once their discounts are applied. Called while the account page renders

hypotheses.subject: io-pricing
hypotheses.summary: If pricing.io-internal.svc were instead found to be operated by a separate company rather than checkout-platform, this same latency signature would instead indicate an upstream (third-party) dependency failure - but the service register places it internally, so this is a fallback only.

supporting_evidence.claim: io-pricing: internal, owned by checkout-platform, at pricing.io-internal.svc
